title: WPMS/3041/2016 of Murari Singh Vs State Of U.p. AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 3041 of 2016
Murari Singh
 ÖÖÖÖ.Petitioner
Versus
State of U.P. and another
 ÖÖ...Respondents
Present : Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate for the petitioner.
Ms. Bina Pandey, Additional Chief Standing Counsel for
the State of U.P./respondents.

Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 The petitioner who was a class IV employee in
Irrigation Department of the State of Uttar Pradesh
reached the age of superannuation and retired from
service on 31.08.2014. During the period of service, he
was allotted an official accommodation in Irrigation
Colony, Mayapur, Haridwar. Under the rules, which are
admitted to the petitioner, after retirement he could
have retained the official accommodation for a
maximum period of one month i.e. till 31.09.2014. The
petitioner, however, continued to retain the same even
thereafter and ultimately vacated the premises on
01.12.2015. In other words, he was occupying the
official accommodation without any authority of law
from 01.10.2014 to 01.12.2015. Consequently a penal
rent is being demanded from the petitioner for
unauthorizedly occupying the official accommodation
from 01.10.2014 to 01.12.2015. Aggrieved, the
petitioner has filed the present petition.
2. The only case of the petitioner before this
Court is that the petitionerís son was also in service and
was residing with the petitioner. The accommodation

2
which was allotted to the petitioner was subsequently
ordered for allotment to one Pradeep Kumar Mittal, who
did not take possession of the said accommodation.
Consequently, the petitionerís son requested the
department that the accommodation earlier allotted to
his father may now be allotted in his favour, which has
not been done.
3. This ground of the petitioner is absolutely
flimsy. An employee must vacate the official
accommodation as per rules after he reaches the age of
superannuation and retires from service, otherwise the
rules provides for penal rent to be recovered from him.
4. Since the petitioner failed to vacate the official
accommodation after his retirement from service, the
penal rent is being recovered from him as per rules,
which requires no interference by this Court.
5. Consequently, writ petition fails and is hereby
dismissed.
